title: kvcache-prefetch-miss-amplification-safeguards-and-slow-path-fallbacks
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Follow-up on an incident where the KV cache prefetch subsystem amplified a transient miss pattern into an eviction/capacity surge. This ticket scopes detection, immediate mitigations, and long-term fixes to prevent repeat amplification across multitenant clusters.
incident_summary: On 2026-02-24 a sudden spike in prefixcache prefetch requests caused excessive insert churn and eviction storms in staging and one small prod shard. Root symptoms: prefetch scheduler mis-classified a rolling churn of cold keys as hot, triggering aggressive prefetches that filled slabs and forced bulk evictions. Resulted in transient latency increases and ~12% increase in token-serving cost for affected customers for the 18m window.
root_cause: The prefetch heuristic (hot-score window = 30s, sample size = 256) was tuned for steady workloads; with a recent client-side throughput pattern (many short-lived keys from a new SDK beta), the heuristic produced false positives. Combined with an unthrottled async prefetch worker pool and an insertion fast-path that bypassed eviction smoothing, the system executed a wave of prefetches that saturated local slab memory and caused eviction storms.
impact: Medium. Affected ~3 nodes in shard-22 for 18 minutes; some tenants experienced 200-400ms tail latency spikes. No data loss. Observability: increased eviction_rate metric, growth in slab_write_bytes, elevated 95/99 P99 token latency on shard. Billing anomaly alert fired (cost delta +12% on affected shard).
timeline: 2026-02-24 09:11 UTC: Alert - eviction_rate on shard-22 exceeded 2x baseline
2026-02-24 09:14 UTC: Oncall triage - identified correlated prefetch spikes in telemetry
2026-02-24 09:18 UTC: Scaled down prefetch worker pool on shard-22 as mitigation (manual config change)
2026-02-24 09:27 UTC: Latency and eviction rates began returning to baseline after worker throttle
2026-02-24 10:00 UTC: Post-incident bridge - initial hypotheses collected and artifact links shared
2026-02-25 15:30 UTC: Root cause confirmed after replaying workload in staging with instrumentation
decisions: Immediately cap concurrent prefetch workers per shard to 8 and add a soft token-bucket with 200 req/s cap per tenant (short-term mitigation)
Add a prefetch-confidence score and require 2 independent hot-signals (frequency + recency) before issuing multi-key prefetches (medium-term fix)
Implement a slow-path fallback: if insertion rate > X and eviction_rate rising, route prefetches to a delayed queue and enable conservative insertion path
action_items: LZ: Deploy worker-pool cap + token-bucket emergency config to all prod shards. Due: 2026-03-05
AP: Instrument prefetch decision path to emit confidence_score, include sample of keys for offline analysis. Due: 2026-03-08
MR: Prototype 2-signal prefetch heuristic (frequency + recent-hit-ratio) and run A/B in staging. Due: 2026-03-15
JC: Implement eviction-smoothing fast-path toggle (adds jitter to inserts when slab pressure > threshold). Due: 2026-03-19
SD: Add dashboard tile and alert for prefetch_amplification_ratio and link to runbook. Due: 2026-03-10
LZ + AP: Update incident runbook with steps to identify prefetch amplification and immediate mitigations. Due: 2026-03-12
notes: This incident was more visible in a small subset of shards with a particular SDK client pattern. Consider engaging SDK team to determine whether beta behavior is expected.
We intentionally avoided a full restart as mitigation; throttling was sufficient and safer for multi-tenant stability.
Security review not required for these changes (no sensitive data handling changes), but quota changes will need product communication.
